full_judgment:
At the instance of the plaintiff-opposite party-petitioner, the Rule was issued by this Court with the following terms: 

 2. Facts leading to the issuance of the Rule are inter alia that the petitioner being plaintiff filed Partition Suit No. 2457 of 2016 before the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Pabna on 6-11-2016. The plaintiff also filed an application under Order 39, rule 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, in short 'the CPC'. Having received the summons, the defendant-opposite party entered appearance in the suit and filed an application for abatement of Partition Suit. The learned Senior Assistant Judge took both the applications and upon hearing, rejected the applications filed by the defendant for abatement and allowed the application for temporary injunction. Thereafter, the defendant filed Miscellaneous Appeal No. 12 of 2017 against the order of temporary injunction and also filed revisional application under section 115(2) of the CPC questioning the legality of the order of rejecting the abatement petition. After hearing both the appeal and revisional application, the learned Additional District Judge was pleased to abate the original partition suit and vacate the order of temporary injunction and by allowing Miscellaneous Appeal dismissed the judgment and order dated 28-5-2017 passed in Partition Suit No. 2457 of 2016. Challenging the legality and propriety of the aforesaid order of temporary injunction, the petitioner moved this Court and obtained the Rule and status quo therewith. 

 "Taking a cue from a reported decision (1986 BLD 326) that in the present day scarcity of accommodation in urban areas a person in possession should not be deprived of using the land for making construction at his own risk and having noticed that the suit land is situated within the Sylhet Municipal area, the High Court Division observed that having regard to the nature of the plaintiffs' claim to the suit land, they had neither a prima facie nor arguable case." 

 "In urban area no co-sharer should be restrained by injunction from making construction. There could not be any second opinion to the authorities on the principle. But the principle cannot be extended to cover a case where very right to construction is based on a deed which is tainted by fraud as has been rightly found by the High Court Division. The said Division did not commit any error or illegality in finding that the plaintiffs have been able to prove the prima facie and arguable case and balance of convenience and inconvenience is in favour of the plaintiff and rightly directed to maintain status quo and to dispose of the suit in six months."
